note: Both sets are drawn from the same wiring schedule rows and are essentially identical: 14 of the 15 claims match exactly, and the only difference (Set A's 151 conductor claim with AL/ARMORED CABLE conditions vs Set B's 151 'conductor quantity and size' claim) is correct in both forms. All values are bound to the right symbol rows per the image (e.g., 150 = AL: 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C.; 33 = CU: 6#10, #10G., 1"C.; 32 = CU: 2#10USE-2), and quotes support the claims. Both sets leave out the same facts, notably symbol row 34 (CU: 6#10, 3#10G., 1"C.), row 10 (CU: #12/2WG.), and several conduit sizes (31: 3/4"C., 20: 3/4"C., 150: 2-1/2"C., 50: 1"C.).
remarks: Text layer is garbled and out of order (symbol numbers detached from their description strings, 'MAIN BONDI' truncated, '00A/2P NFDS' cut off at the left margin), so the image table was used as the authority. Both sets name the same kind of entity inconsistently ('Circuit 33' vs 'Wiring Schedule 150' for symbol numbers in the SYMBOL column); normalizing this would help. Both sets also omit the NOTES block (main panel MP, 120/240V, 1-phase 3W, 50A/2P main breaker, 200A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R enclosure), which contains real engineering facts.
